title: Now Gird Your Patient Loins Again
description: Now Gird Your Patient Loins Again in Tonic Solfa to ALL SAINTS, NEW, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: William Croswell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 451, “Hymn for Christmas”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ALL SAINTS, NEW; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now gird your pa-tient loins a-gain, Your wast-ing torch-es trim! The chief of all the sons of men, Shall we not wel-come him? Fill all his courts with sa-cred songs, And from the tem-ple wall Wave gar-lands o'er the joy-ful throngs That crowd his fes-ti-val!

lines: Now gird your patient loins again,
The chief of all the sons of men,
Fill all his courts with sacred songs,
Wave garlands o'er the joyful throngs
And still more freshly in the mind
Which then were born for all mankind,
In every heart that him receives,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Croswell died in 1851.
credits: Words by William Croswell (1804–1851), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ALL SAINTS, NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
